questions.question: Radha can complete a piece of work in 3 days, while Raji can complete the same work in 2 days. Both of them complete this work by working together and get ₹150 as total payment for the work done. What is the share of Radha out of the above payment?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

Radha can complete a piece of work in 3 days, while Raji can complete the same work in 2 days. Both of them complete this work by working together and get ₹150 as total payment for the work done.

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM

Time =( Work)/(Efficiency)

Ratio of x and y is (x)/(y)

**Calculation:**

Work done by Radha in one day is (1)/(3) 

Work done by Raji in one day is (1)/(2) 

Hence, the ratio of their contribution to daily work is (2)/(3)

Let Radha's pay be x and Raji's pay be 150 - x.

Then, (x)/(150-x)=(2)/(3)

Solving for x,

3x=300-2x

x=(300)/(5)=60

**∴ Radha's pay is ₹ 60**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

LCM of (2, 3) = 6 = Total Work

Efficiency =frac{ Work} { Time}

Efficiency of Radha =(6)/(3) = 2

Efficiency of Raji = (6)/(2) = 3

Since payment will be done according to the efficiency so,

Radha's pay = (Radha Efficiency)/(Total Efficiency)times Total Payment

Radha' pay = (2)/(5)×150 = ₹ 60

questions.question: X and Y together can do a piece of work in 30 days. Z alone can do it in 60 days. If they worked together, then in how many days they can finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

X and Y can do a work in 30 days, Z can do it alone in 60 days.

Formula:

(1/(X+Y)) + (1/Z) = 1/Total

Calculation:

⇒ (1/30) + (1/60) = 1/Total

⇒ Total = 20 days.

Hence, they can finish the work in 20 days.

questions.question: P. Q and R alone can complete a piece of work in 30 hours, 10 hours and 15 hours respectively. In how much time they will finish the work, if they worked together?
questions.solution:

P. Q and R alone can complete a piece of work in 30 hours, 10 hours, and 15 hours respectively

Concept used:

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day

The efficiency of P is 60 / 30 = 2 units

The efficiency of Q is 60 / 10 = 6 units

The efficiency of R is 60 / 15 = 4 units

Total efficiency of P. Q and R is 2 + 6 + 4 = 12 units

⇒ 60 / 12 hours = 5 hours

**∴ The correct option is 1**

questions.question: X and Y together can do a work in 10 days. Y and Z together can do the same work in 15 days. Z and X together can do the same work in 12 days. In how many days can Z alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given**:

X and Y can complete a work in 10 days.

Y and Z can complete a work in 15 days.

Z and X can complete a work in 12 days.

**Formula used:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation: **

X and Y can complete a work in 10 days.

Y and Z can complete a work in 15 days.

Z and X can complete a work in 12 days.

Let the total work be 60 units. (LCM of 10, 15, and 12).

Efficiency of X and Y = 60/10 = 6 units/day.....(1)

Efficiency of Y and Z = 60/15 = 4 units/day.....(2)

Efficiency of Z and X = 60/12 = 5 units/day.....(3)

From (1), (2) and (3), we get

]Efficiency of Z = 15/2 - 6 = 3/2 = 1.5 units/day 

Time taken by Z to complete the work 

= 60/1.5 

= 600/15 = 40 days

**Z can alone do the work for 40 days.**

questions.question: A can do a certain work in 30 days. B is 25% more efficient than A, and C is 20% more efficient than B. A and B work together for 10 days. C alone completes the remaining work in x days. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A = 30 days 

Efficiency of B = 25% more than A

Efficiency of C = 20% more than B

**Formula used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time taken 

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of A be = 100 

⇒ Efficiency of B will be = 125

⇒ Efficiency of C will be = 150 

∴ Ratio of efficiencies of A, B and C is 100 : 125 : 150 respectively. 

⇒ A : B : C = 4 : 5 : 6 

Total Work = 4 × 30 = 120 units 

Work done by A and B in 10 days = (4 + 5) × 10 = 90 

⇒ Remaining work = 120 - 90 = 30 units 

C did the remaining work in x days, so x days = 30 units/6 

⇒ x days = 5 days 

**∴ The required result is 5 days. **

questions.question: If A and B can do a piece of work in 20 days, and A alone can do the same work in 30 days, then in how many days can B alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A and B to do a piece of work = 20 days

Time taken by A alone to do the same work = 30 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 20 and 30 is 60

Efficiency of A and B = (60/20) = 3 units/day

Efficiency of A = (60/30) = 2 units/day

Then,

Time taken by B alone to complete the same work = [(60/(3 – 2)]

⇒ 60/1

⇒ 60 days

**∴ The required time taken by B is 60 days**

questions.question: Ram can do a piece of work in 18 hours. Shyam and Naresh can do it in 9 hours. Ram and Naresh can do it in 12 hours. How long will Shyam alone take to do it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ram can do a piece of work in 18 hours.

Shyam and Naresh together can do it in 9 hours.

Ram and Naresh together can do it in 12 hours.

**Formula Used:**

If A can do a piece of work in x hours and B can do the same work in y hours, then together they can do it in (1)/(frac{1){x}+(1)/(y)} hours.

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be the LCM of 18, 9, and 12, which is 36 units.

Efficiency of Ram = (36)/(18) = 2 units/hour

Efficiency of Shyam and Naresh together = (36)/(9) = 4 units/hour

Efficiency of Ram and Naresh together = (36)/(12) = 3 units/hour

Let the efficiency of Naresh be N units/hour.

Then, the efficiency of Shyam = (4 - N) units/hour.

Since Ram and Naresh together do 3 units/hour and Ram's efficiency is 2 units/hour,

⇒ N = 3 - 2 = 1 unit/hour

So, the efficiency of Shyam = 4 - 1 = 3 units/hour.

Time taken by Shyam alone to do the work = (Total\:Work)/(Efficiency\:of\:Shyam) = (36)/(3) = 12 hours

**Shyam alone will take 12 hours to do the work.**
